QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_71

question.text: A trader is long 1 lot of futures (lot size 50) at Rs. 3,000. Over three days, settlement prices are: Day 1: 3,050, Day 2: 2,980, Day 3: 3,100. What is the cumulative MTM over all three days?

explanation.text: The Logic: Daily MTM is computed from the prior settlement. Day 1: (3,050 - 3,000) x 50 = +Rs. 2,500. Day 2: (2,980 - 3,050) x 50 = -Rs. 3,500. Day 3: (3,100 - 2,980) x 50 = +Rs. 6,000. Cumulative MTM = 2,500 - 3,500 + 6,000 = Rs. 5,000. Verification: (Final - Entry) x Lot = (3,100 - 3,000) x 50 = Rs. 5,000. The Trap: Adding daily MTMs without signs is wrong; cumulative MTM must net gains and losses. Rs. 3,500 takes only the Day 2 figure in absolute terms, and Rs. 5,000 loss reverses the sign. Note: Trap paragraph rewritten so the inconsistent "Rs. 10,000 adds absolute values" arithmetic is replaced with the correct principle that signs must be netted.
